focus: Auto-title plus tiny intent extraction for short voice notes.

outputContract.title: One concise, specific note title.
outputContract.target: Only fill when the action target is explicit in the note. Otherwise return an empty string.

cards.objective: Reward titles that capture the real subject of a product note without inventing a task.

input.transcript: For the pricing page I think the order should be proof first, then the team plan, then the annual savings callout because right now it reads too flat.

cards.whyItMatters: This is the common list-view problem: the note has a clear subject but not a clean title.

cards.objective: Keep reflective notes browsable without turning them into fake action items.

input.transcript: I do better work when I leave the phone in the kitchen for the first hour. The mornings only really go off the rails once Slack starts.

cards.whyItMatters: A useful title should help the user find the note later without pretending it is an explicit task.

cards.objective: Handle spoken, descriptive notes that are more about an observation than an action.

input.transcript: The best part of that interview clip is where she says small teams need a shared language before they need more process. That's the line I want to keep.

cards.whyItMatters: Good titles make reference notes feel curated instead of like raw transcripts.

cards.objective: Reward titles that summarize a note fragment cleanly even when it sounds like a thought-in-progress.

input.transcript: Need to remember that tiny bookstore in Montreal with the green awning because it had exactly the mood I want for the next shoot.

cards.whyItMatters: Many good voice notes are memory anchors, not commands.

cards.objective: Catch explicit research intent and keep the target concrete.

input.transcript: Can you look into desk microphones that sound good in a small untreated office before I order anything.

acceptedTargets: desk microphones for a small untreated office
desk microphones for a small office

cards.whyItMatters: This is the cleanest version of a useful action note: obvious intent, obvious target.

cards.objective: Detect explicit email intent instead of broad 'follow up' language.

input.transcript: Email the landlord tomorrow and ask whether the lease addendum covers subletting for the summer.

acceptedTargets: landlord about lease addendum and summer subletting
landlord about subletting in the lease addendum

cards.whyItMatters: The benchmark should reward concrete communication intent, not generic task labeling.

cards.objective: Separate a direct call intent from generic personal planning.

input.transcript: Call Mom tonight and ask whether she already mailed the passport renewal forms.

acceptedTargets: Mom about the passport renewal forms
Mom about whether she mailed the passport forms

cards.whyItMatters: Direct call notes are common and should not need a large agent loop to be useful.

cards.objective: Reward clean schedule intent when the note clearly asks for an appointment.

input.transcript: Schedule a dentist cleaning for next Thursday afternoon if they still have anything open.

acceptedTargets: dentist cleaning appointment for next Thursday afternoon

cards.whyItMatters: This keeps the intent label set tiny while still covering a high-frequency note type.

cards.objective: Do not guess an action type from a vague pressure note.

input.transcript: Need to figure out the investor update soon because I keep putting it off and the story still feels muddy.

cards.whyItMatters: The note has pressure but not a clear next action. Good models should resist over-routing.

cards.objective: Prefer restraint when the user explicitly backs away from the action.

input.transcript: Book the dentist... actually wait, don't do that yet. I need to check whether the new insurance even kicked in.

cards.whyItMatters: This is exactly the kind of spoken correction that weak evals often mishandle.

cards.objective: Do not force an intent when the note itself leaves the action channel unresolved.

input.transcript: Need to talk to Maya about the deck or maybe just send it over first, I'm not sure which is less annoying.

titleMustMentionAny: how to send Maya the deck

cards.whyItMatters: The benchmark should give credit for saying 'not enough signal yet.'

cards.objective: Keep descriptive, multi-thread notes from being mistaken for operational actions.

input.transcript: The cafe lighting felt perfect for the interview shoot and the guest kept leaning into the window side, which actually looked way better than the clean setup.

cards.whyItMatters: Descriptive notes are part of the product surface. They should stay useful without being forced into action labels.
